 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment
Heard Sri.M.B.Chandrachooda, learned counsel for appellant.
Also heard Sri.Harsha Kumar Gowda H.R., learned counsel for respondent No.1.
There is no representation on the side of respondent No.2.
There was no representation even on 25.10.2024.
Therefore, the matter is taken up for pronouncement of judgment.

2. Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Bengaluru in MVC No.1616/2019 dated 05.01.2021.
This is a claimant's appeal.

3. As against the claim for Rs.25,00,000/- in total, the Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of NC: 2024:KHC:45217 Rs.4,34,353/- as compensation and aggrieved by the same,
the present appeal is filed.
4. Sri
.M.B.Chandachooda, arguing the matter, contends that the appellant sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
He took extensive treatment and during the course of treatment he also underwent a surgery.
Though sufficient proof was produced to establish the nature of injuries sustained, the treatment taken and the aspect of disability, the Tribunal failed to award just compensation.
Learned counsel also submits that the appellant, as a vegetable vendor was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal took the notional income as Rs.9,000/- per month which is erroneous.

Learned counsel also contends that the accident occurred in the year 2019 and for the relevant period the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as Rs.14,000/- per month for settlement of claims and atleast said figure should have been considered by the Tribunal.
Learned counsel thereby seeks for enhancement of compensation.
5. Sri.

Harsha Kumar Gowda H.R., learned counsel for respondent No.1 states that the offending vehicle was validly NC: 2024:KHC:45217 insured with respondent No.2 and the insurance policy stood in force by the date of accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly fastened the liability upon respondent No.2 and hence necessary orders may be passed.

sentences.text: 2 6. By all the evidence brought on record, the appellant succeeded in establishing that he sustained fracture of shaft of femur right, pelvis fracture bilateral and internal derangement of knee right.
The appellant also established through the evidence of PW2 that the disability in respect of right lower limb is 61%.
The tribunal, evaluating the evidence that is produced, took the disability in respect of whole body as 15%.
The said observation needs no interference.
So far as the occupation and earnings of the appellant by the date of accident is concerned, the appellant failed to produce any authentic proof that he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
However, the submission that is made by learned counsel for appellant to take the notional income as Rs.14,000/- is convincing.
Therefore, the notional income of the appellant is taken as Rs.14,000/- per month.
Admittedly, the appellant was aged about 41 years by the date of accident.
The disability as assessed by the Tribunal as earlier indicated is 15% in respect of whole body which is permanent NC: 2024:KHC:45217 in nature.

Therefore, 25% of the earnings are required to be added towards future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier '14'.

Therefore, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to under the head loss of future earnings is as under:

 Loss of future earnings,

7.
Having considered the nature of injuries sustained, this Court is of the view that the appellant would not have attended his normal pursuits atleast for a period of four months.

Thus, loss of earnings during laid up period comes to Rs.56,000/- (Rs.14,000/- x 4).
NC: 2024:KHC:45217 8.

Having considered the nature of injuries sustained, the treatment taken and disability with which the appellant was left with, this Court is of the view that the appellant is entitled to compensation under the following heads:

sentences.text: Sl . Heads of compensation Amount in No Rs.
1 Compensation for pain an 50,000-00 suffering 2
Medical expenses 1,02,553-00 3

Towards food, extra nourishment, conveyance 20,000-00 and attendant charges 4 Loss of future earnings 4,41,000-00 5 Loss of earnings during laid 56,000-00 up period 6 Loss of amenities in life 20,000-00 7
Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total 07,09,553-00 9.

Thus, the foregoing discussion makes it clear that the amount that is awarded by the Tribunal i.e.,
Rs.4,34,353/- is required to be enhanced.
The appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.7,09,553/- as compensation.

10. Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2024:KHC:45217 ii) The compensation that is awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, through orders in MVC No.1616/2019 dated 05.01.2021 is enhanced from Rs.4,34,353/- to Rs.07,09,553/-.
iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to answer the claim.
v) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
(DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) JUDGE AP
